title: Genetically Modified Organisms, Enzyme and Protein Engineering
shortDescription: What GMOs are, how they are regulated in India, and how enzymes and proteins are redesigned for industry.
genZNote: Edit the gene, change the crop — then deal with the regulator. India's GM story is short: Bt cotton yes, most else is still in the waiting room.

sections.heading: GMOs in Food
bullets: GMO: organism whose genome has been altered by recombinant DNA (transgene insertion, gene editing). Examples: Bt cotton/maize (Bacillus thuringiensis toxin), herbicide-tolerant soybean, golden rice (β-carotene), Flavr Savr tomato (first commercial GM food, 1994), recombinant chymosin for cheese (1990).
Techniques: Agrobacterium-mediated transfer, gene gun, CRISPR-Cas9; markers and promoters.

India: GEAC (under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change) approves GM organisms; Bt cotton (2002) is the only GM crop approved for commercial cultivation; GM mustard environmental release was cleared by GEAC in 2022 but is under judicial review; the Supreme Court in 2024 asked for a national policy on GM crops. FSSAI regulates GM foods in the food chain and labelling is being operationalised — verify current rules.
Debate: benefits (yield, pest resistance, nutrition) vs concerns (allergenicity, gene flow, biodiversity, labelling and trade).

sections.heading: Enzyme and Protein Engineering
bullets: Aims: improve activity, stability (heat/pH), specificity or reduce inhibition.

Methods: rational design (site-directed mutagenesis), directed evolution (random mutation + screening; Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2018 to Frances Arnold), recombinant expression in E. coli, Bacillus, Aspergillus, Pichia.
Immobilisation: adsorption, entrapment, covalent binding, cross-linking, encapsulation for reuse (e.g. glucose isomerase for HFCS; lactase for lactose-free milk).

Applications: cheese (recombinant chymosin), detergents, baking (xylanase), brewing, low-lactose dairy, de-bittering, protein hydrolysates and bioactive peptides; engineered proteins for texture (heme proteins in plant-based meat).

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: GMOs and engineered enzymes and proteins apply recombinant DNA and protein design to improve crops and food processing under biosafety regulation.
keyFacts: Bt cotton (2002) only commercial GM crop.
Recombinant chymosin: first GM enzyme in food.

commonTraps: Do not say Bt brinjal is cultivated in India — a moratorium applies.

questions.prompt: Bt in Bt cotton stands for:
questions.explanation: The Bt gene comes from B. thuringiensis.
